standard.title: Geo-Synthetics — Geo-Textiles Used as Protection (or Cushioning) Materials — Specification
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling protocols, and testing methods for nonwoven and woven geotextiles used as protective (or cushioning) layers. These materials are placed directly over geomembranes or other impermeable liners in civil and geotechnical engineering projects (such as municipal landfills, industrial effluent containment ponds, canals, reservoirs, and reservoirs) to prevent mechanical puncture, tearing, or localized stress concentrations from sharp aggregates and subgrade defects.

version.current_version: First Edition, 2013 (reaffirmed periodically; incorporating Amendment No. 1, December 2023)

amendments.summary: Substitutes Clause 4.3 (fourth sentence) to enforce strict carbon black and stabilizer composition limits on polyolefin fibers. It also replaces Table 1 to update mechanical and physical characteristics, deletes legacy reference standards, and inserts modern test method specifications such as wide-width tensile and CBR static puncture tests.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Geo Textiles (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all geotextiles used as protection (or cushioning) materials must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Export-only products are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymers and technical textiles.
requirements: Every roll or bundle of cushioning geotextiles conforming to the requirements of this standard must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).

After undergoing 500 hours of continuous ultraviolet light exposure in a Xenon-arc apparatus as prescribed in IS 13162 (Part 2), all types of protection geotextiles must maintain a minimum tensile strength retention of 70 percent.
Geotextiles are graded by mass per unit area (GSM) ranging from 300 g/m² to 1200 g/m² depending on project-specific cushioning and physical demands.

Mechanical properties must comply with the strict parameters defined in Table 1, including wide-width tensile strength (IS 16635) and static puncture resistance (CBR test under IS 16078) to survive localized shear stresses.

Each roll must be legibly and indelibly marked or labeled with: a) Manufacturer's name or trademark; b) Grade, width, and length of roll; c) Batch or lot number with date of manufacture; and d) Nominal mass per unit area (g/m²).
